clue.text: Clumsy joke right away had Den worried

indicators.note: away tells us the right-hand letter is sent off from the joke word

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack or joke

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters of had and Den are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy gag goes down badly, leaving a man called Den anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from CRACK, leaving CACK; 'worried' rearranges HAD and DEN into HANDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cack-handed is informal British slang for awkward or inept with the hands.

clue.text: Lovely draw in competition: Italy against Spain

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so one code sits beside the other
in places the drawn match inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition, such as the FA Cup
a tie is a drawn match
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A sweet football draw in a cup tie between Italy and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovely, used as a noun, is an attractive person, which matches the affectionate term for a sweetheart.

clue.text: Fresh director supports head of casting

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits below it
head of picks the top letter of the word casting

parts.note: David Lean was the film director of Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A new film director takes charge of casting.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean and fresh are synonyms for unused or unsoiled, as in a fresh sheet.

clue.text: Heave second wife onto robust beast

parts.note: to hump is to heave or lug something heavy
to second a proposal is to back it
hale means robust and healthy

explanation.surface: Someone lifts their spouse onto a strong animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This large whale, known for its song, is a huge marine beast.

clue.text: Record includes dream about iconic structure

indicators.note: includes means the record word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to note something is to record it

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of dream are moved around

explanation.surface: A written record holds a dream about a famous building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the dream into REDAM before 'includes' wraps the record round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cathedral is one of the most famous buildings in the world, an example of an iconic structure.

clue.text: Animal close to home territory

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of home

parts.note: land is territory

explanation.surface: A creature lives near its home turf.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: No chance of single female hosting confirmation in Rome

indicators.note: hosting means the first pair of letters takes the other in as a guest

parts.note: a means one, a single item
si is Italian for yes

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman holding a church confirmation in Rome has little hope.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of disbelief is an idiom meaning it will never happen.

clue.text: Clever-clever well-heeled Star Wars actor

parts.note: smart means stylish and well dressed, like the well-heeled
Alec Guinness played Obi-Wan Kenobi in Star Wars

explanation.surface: A wealthy, too-clever Star Wars performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all who shows off their cleverness is described with this idiom, matching the sarcastic doubled adjective.

clue.text: Don't believe this cook to be 'iding fish?

indicators.note: to be hiding, with its h dropped, says one word hides the other inside it

parts.note: to fry is to cook
the fish hake, with its h dropped as in 'iding, gives 'ake

explanation.surface: A Cockney cook is told to hide some fish, which sounds suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in ''iding' is the hint that the fish (hake) drops its h too, as a Cockney would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fakery is sham or deception, something one should not trust.

clue.text: Unit at health centre finally has room

indicators.note: finally takes the end letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A clinic department finally gets a room of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in measuring gas supply.

clue.text: Signature works returned by country (not Norway)

indicators.note: returned means the works word is read backwards

parts.note: art means works, as in works of art

indicators.note: not means the Norway letter is left out

parts.note: Denmark is a country
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A trade embargo hits signature pieces sent back from a Scandinavian country.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature style or feature is a distinctive hallmark, the thing a person or firm is known for.

clue.text: Easily agree best rental being good at accommodation

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, describing someone happy to oblige

indicators.note: easily hints at letters that move freely into a new order

parts.note: top means best
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A tenant readily agrees to the best rental, as the flat is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Being accommodating means willingly fitting in with others' wishes, the eagerness to oblige.

clue.text: Honour Geordie comedian after Tyneside comeback?

indicators.note: after places the comedian's name behind the region's letters
comeback means the region's letters come back, read in reverse

parts.note: NE stands for north-east England, home of Tyneside
Ross Noble is a stand-up comedian from Newcastle (a Geordie is a Tynesider)

explanation.surface: A Newcastle comic is honoured after a return to his home region.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to honour someone by raising them to the peerage.

clue.text: Feature on short Venetian official as a shining example

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the feature word after the official

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice; short drops its last letter
to feature in a film is to star

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature on a Venetian dignitary holds him up as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, literally an example of something shining.

clue.text: Name of man in charge stocking small battery

indicators.note: stocking means the in-charge letters hold the others in stock

parts.note: AA is a common battery size

explanation.surface: A man in charge of a shop stocks small batteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's first name, as borne by Isaac Newton.

clue.text: Possibly fly east from land getting work in bar

indicators.note: from means the east letter is taken away from the land word

parts.note: earth means land or ground

indicators.note: in puts the work inside the bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A fly might head east from land to find work in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes E from EARTH, leaving ARTH. 'Possibly' says a fly is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects such as flies belong to the phylum of jointed-legged invertebrates, so a fly is one example.

clue.text: Dizzy maid regularly leaving treacle for butterfly

indicators.note: dizzy suggests the letters of maid spin into a new order
regularly leaving means taking every other letter of treacle, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A light-headed housemaid swaps treacle for a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dizzy' rearranges MAID into ADMI; every second letter of TREACLE gives RAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a common butterfly, often called simply by its last word.

clue.text: Dreadful sitcom has one suffering

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a bad state, mixed up

explanation.surface: Watching a terrible sitcom makes someone suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Masochists take pleasure in their own pain, so they are people who seek out suffering.

clue.text: Some acres Sid acquired for Dick?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone named Sid bought land on behalf of someone named Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: Cressida Dick was London's Metropolitan Police Commissioner, so the hidden first name is what goes before the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Metropolitan Police Commissioner's first name goes with the surname Dick, so the clue asks which first name goes before it.

clue.text: Urbanites keep going into river

indicators.note: going into means the keep word enters the river

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
to keep something is to own it

explanation.surface: City dwellers keep on walking into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep going' reads as one phrase, but 'going into' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Townees are people who live in towns, the informal word for urban dwellers.

clue.text: Take place in middle of row C with dog

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of row

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Find a seat in the middle of row C with a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen, the same as an event taking place.

clue.text: Fasten together basic material

definitions.meaning: to fix sheets with a bent wire clip
a raw material or basic food item that is a mainstay

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to clip papers with a wire fastener and a main commodity or basic item.

clue.text: Turnover across the car retailers building

indicators.note: turnover says the run of letters is turned over, read backwards
across signals letters running across the words that follow

explanation.surface: Turnover at the car dealers' premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like business jargon but is the reversal signal; 'across' marks the hidden letters ECARRET.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, a type of building.

clue.text: Wear down Queen with poem

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: The Queen is worn out by a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water does to rock.

clue.text: Pieces of cloth left buried among islands by Turks

indicators.note: buried among means the left letter is set inside the islands' name

parts.note: the Caicos islands are paired with the Turks islands in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Bits of fabric are abandoned and buried on Turkish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turks' suggests Turkey, but it is part of the Turks and Caicos Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton fabric, so pieces of it are calicos.

clue.text: Limits to clinical index reflecting height gain

indicators.note: limits to means the first and last letters of clinical
reflecting means the index's letters are read in mirror order

parts.note: BMI is the body mass index, a clinical measure

explanation.surface: Limits on a clinical index show a gain in height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clinical index' reads as one measure, but 'clinical' gives its outer letters and 'index' is BMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent, an increase in altitude.

clue.text: Burst pipe blocked with old Argentinian meat

indicators.note: blocked with means the scrambled pipe is stopped up by the other piece inside it
burst suggests the pipe's letters are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: Juan Perón was a former president of Argentina

explanation.surface: A burst pipe is clogged with an old Argentinian's meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burst' makes PEPI, which 'blocked with' then splits open around the president's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage, a cured meat often found on pizza.

clue.text: Calf and tibia discovered to be explanation of movements

indicators.note: discovered means each word loses its covering, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Uncovered leg bones explain how someone moved.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an account of where someone was at the time of a crime, explaining their whereabouts.

clue.text: Twister perhaps played … brandy's two-thirds gone

indicators.note: two-thirds gone means each of the two words loses its first two-thirds, keeping only the final third

explanation.surface: Someone played a game of Twister after most of the brandy was drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAYED keeps ED and BRANDY keeps DY once two-thirds of each goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of air or water, of which a twister is a violent example.

clue.text: Fix hat before beginning to add fashion accessory

indicators.note: fix suggests the letters are put into a new arrangement
beginning to takes the first letter of add

explanation.surface: Adjust a hat before adding a fashion accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a link word placing hat first, but it is part of the anagram fodder for 'Fix'.
explanation.definitionFit: This long fluffy scarf of plumes is a fashion accessory worn round the neck.
